title: Rigveda 10.173: Hymn for a king
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.173: Hymn for a king: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.173 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to consecration of a king. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 148v-149v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.173.1-5 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 31); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 149r
translation.original_text:
1ā tvā̍hārṣam a̱ntar e̍dhi dhru̱vas ti̱ṣṭhāvi̍cācaliḥ | viśa̍s tvā̱ sarvā̍ vāñchantu̱ mā tvad rā̱ṣṭram adhi̍ bhraśat ||
2i̱haivaidhi̱ māpa̍ cyoṣṭhā̱ḥ parva̍ta i̱vāvi̍cācaliḥ | indra̍ ive̱ha dhru̱vas ti̍ṣṭhe̱ha rā̱ṣṭram u̍ dhāraya ||
3i̱mam indro̍ adīdharad dhru̱vaṁ dhru̱veṇa̍ ha̱viṣā̍ | tasmai̱ somo̱ adhi̍ brava̱t tasmā̍ u̱ brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̍ḥ ||
4dhru̱vā dyaur dhru̱vā pṛ̍thi̱vī dhru̱vāsa̱ḥ parva̍tā i̱me | dhru̱vaṁ viśva̍m i̱daṁ jaga̍d dhru̱vo rājā̍ vi̱śām a̱yam ||
5dhru̱vaṁ te̱ rājā̱ varu̍ṇo dhru̱vaṁ de̱vo bṛha̱spati̍ḥ | dhru̱vaṁ ta̱ indra̍ś cā̱gniś ca̍ rā̱ṣṭraṁ dhā̍rayatāṁ dhru̱vam ||
translation.text:
1BE with us; I have chosen thee: stand stedfast and immovable. Let all the people wish for thee let not thy kingship fall away.
2Be even here; fall not away be like a mountain unremoved. Stand stedfast here like Indra's self, and hold the kingship in the grasp.
3This man hath Indra stablished, made secure by strong oblation's power. May Soma speak a benison, and Brahmaṇaspati, on him.
4Firm is the sky and firm the earth, and stedfast also are these hills. Stedfast is all this living world, and stedfast is this King of men.
5Stedfast, may Varuṇa the King, stedfast, the God Br̥ihaspati, Stedfast, may Indra, stedfast too, may Agni keep thy stedfast reign.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 149r (OPenn image 148, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.173.1 ‹-tiṣṭhāvicācaliḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 149v, begins in RV 10.173.6 ‹-viśo balihṛtas karat›. Verses 10.173.1-5 end on this page; 10.173.1 begins on fol. 148v.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.173.6 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 31); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 149v
translation.original_text: <sup>6</sup>dhru̱vaṁ dhru̱veṇa̍ ha̱viṣā̱bhi soma̍m mṛśāmasi | atho̍ ta̱ indra̱ḥ keva̍lī̱r viśo̍ bali̱hṛta̍s karat ||
translation.text: <sup>6</sup>On constant Soma let us think with constant sacrificial gift And then may Indra make the clans bring tribute unto thee alone.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 149v (OPenn image 149, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.173.6 ‹-viśo balihṛtas karat›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 150r, begins in RV 10.175.1 ‹-grāvāṇaḥ savitā devaḥ suvatu›. Verse 10.173.6 ends on this page; 10.173.6 begins on fol. 149r.
